state.misconception_label: Believes f(x - a) translates the function up a units

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: What transformation maps the graph of \(y=f(x) \) to the graph of \( y=f(x-3) \). I got Translation by vector
\(
\left[\begin{array}{l}
0 \\
3
\end{array}\right]
\) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: It seems like you're on the right track with thinking about translations, but remember that \(f(x-a)\) actually shifts the graph horizontally, not vertically. Try to think about how changing the input value affects the graph's position along the x-axis. Can you think of how the graph of \(y=f(x)\) would shift if you subtracted 3 from the input?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh, I see! So if I subtract 3 from the input, it actually shifts the graph to the right instead of up? That’s kind of confusing because I thought it would go up. So, would the translation be by the vector \(\left[\begin{array}{l} 3 \\ 0 \end{array}\right]\) instead?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You're making great progress in understanding how the input affects the graph's position. Remember that subtracting from the input value shifts the graph to the right, not up. So yes, the correct translation would be by the vector \(\left[\begin{array}{l} 3 \\ 0 \end{array}\right]\) to represent this horizontal shift. Keep up the good work in identifying and applying these transformations!

score.justification_pass1: While the teacher correctly identifies the horizontal nature of the transformation and the mathematics is accurate, they primarily tell rather than elicit reasoning, and the student's final turn shows acceptance rather than deep understanding of why the counterintuitive direction occurs.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher effectively scaffolds by breaking down the transformation concept into manageable steps (horizontal vs. vertical shifts, input vs. output changes), provides appropriate hints rather than direct answers, and adjusts support by confirming the student's corrected understanding, though could have probed slightly deeper to ensure full conceptual mastery.
